image_description: A close-up, slightly angled view of a white Apple iPod Classic. The device features a rectangular body with rounded corners, a color LCD screen at the top displaying a pink/purple abstract or album art image, and the iconic circular click wheel interface below the screen. The click wheel has a central button and a touch-sensitive ring. A black lanyard or strap is attached to the bottom left corner. The background is blurry, showing what appears to be a patterned surface or fabric.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The click wheel lacks the crisp, sharp labeling (MENU, NEXT/PREV, PLAY/PAUSE) typically found on real iPods. The text appears melted, illegible, or entirely absent, replaced by vague smudges. This is a common AI generation artifact where fine text/details fail to render correctly.
The image on the screen is indistinct and lacks the pixel-sharp clarity expected of a digital display. It resembles a painted texture rather than a lit LCD screen.
The edge of the white casing near the bottom right seems to blend slightly into the background shadow, lacking a hard, defined physical boundary.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific model generation (Classic vs Nano vs Shuffle) and verify class alignment.
To specifically analyze the illegible/melted text on the click wheel, which is a critical functional component.
To check for edge bleeding between the white casing and the background, and ensure the device is a single coherent object.
To evaluate the realism of the screen's glow and the digital nature of the displayed content.

focus_areas: Legibility and correctness of click wheel labels (MENU, etc.)
Sharpness and digital nature of the screen display
Edge definition of the white casing against the background
Geometric symmetry of the circular click wheel
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the click wheel text. Real iPods have very specific, sharp sans-serif lettering. AI often fails here, producing gibberish or smudges. Also, verify if the screen looks like a backlit LCD or just a printed texture. The 'Fits in hand' checkpoint was marked untestable, which is correct, but ensure the scale relative to the lanyard attachment point makes sense for a pocket device.
